paras: The mock hanging of an accused burglar at Nebraska City was an episode in October 1882 in which a party of Nebraska City 'lynchers' repeatedly hanged and revived a man accused of burglary. The man survived and, given the choice between a final hanging and leaving the country, he left. A Connecticut weekly carried the story as an oddity because the lynchers had 'varied the usual course of proceedings'.

According to the only report found, the lynchers hanged the man from a tree limb for a while, took him down, and carefully resuscitated him. They repeated this until, in the paper's words, 'the neck threatened to give out, and all hands were tired.' They then offered him a hanging 'for keeps' or departure from the country, and he chose to leave.

The item gave no name for the man or his attackers, no exact date beyond 'the other day', and no race for anyone involved. It added that there seemed to have been no particular evidence that he had stolen anything.
No report of arrests, an investigation or any official response appears in the coverage found.

The episode is known from a single paragraph in the 'News Items' column of the Willimantic Journal of Connecticut on 27 October 1882, set among local accidents and curiosities. The paper told it in a wry tone, explaining the lynchers' 'leniency' by the fact that the accused was 'not a horsethief, but a burglar'. No account from a Nebraska paper was found.
